title: WoR-Flasher Configuration Schema
description: JSON schema for WoR-Flasher configuration parameters

board.description: Explicit physical board required by the legacy ARM32 IoT Core FFU profile. The IoT workflow resolves its own route; rpiModel is for desktop package selection.

rpiModel.description: Target package route: 3 (Pi 3 or Pi 2 v1.2), 4, or 5. The GUI lists Pi 2 v1.2 separately.

canInstallOnSameDrive.description: Whether to install Windows directly onto target drive (true) or build recovery media (false)

imageFamily.description: Desktop ARM64 ISO/ESD preparation (default) or separate legacy ARM32 IoT Core full-FFU deployment.

architecture.description: Optional architecture assertion: desktop requires arm64; the supported Raspberry Pi IoT Core profile requires arm32. Omit to use the image-family architecture.

downloadIotImage.description: Explicitly download and import the reviewed Microsoft IoT Core package with mandatory TLS/hash checks. Only for imageFamily=iot-core; leave sourceFile empty. No Windows installer is executed.

sourceFile.description: Local desktop Windows ARM64 ISO/ESD, or the reviewed Raspberry Pi IoT Core FFU/ISO/MSI. IoT delivery packages are verified and extracted natively. Raw IMG, unapproved images and ARM64 IoT Core are not accepted.

downloadDir.description: Directory path for downloads and extracted media

useCache.description: Cache mode: 0 (redownload), 1 (reuse with manifest check), 2 (trust cache)

applyCustomConfigTxt.description: Whether to apply custom config.txt to the boot partition

configTxt.description: Body of config.txt for the boot partition

iotHdmiMode.description: IoT-only firmware display timing: recommended 720p60 compatibility (default), unchanged official image, 1080p60, or restricted custom HDMI settings. Explicit selections are preserved. Monitor and OS-driver support still apply.

iotHdmiConfig.description: For iotHdmiMode=custom, ASCII HDMI key=value lines. Require hdmi_group and hdmi_mode; optionally hdmi_force_hotplug and hdmi_drive. Other firmware keys, filters and custom modelines are rejected.

oobeNetworkBypass.description: Whether to hide Windows 11 OOBE network and online-account screens. Ignored for Windows 10.

pi4AutoDisable3Gb.description: Whether to disable 3GB RAM limit on Pi 4 after setup

pi4UefiShellUnlock.description: Whether to use a one-time UEFI Shell handoff to persistently disable the Pi 4 RAM limit

uefiUseLatest.description: Override UEFI selection: true uses the latest stable release, false uses the selected/configured UEFI version. Omit to use latest for Pi 3 and pinned for Pi 4/5.

driversUseLatest.description: Whether to query GitHub for latest drivers instead of the selected/configured driver version

hideEmptyDrives.description: Whether to hide empty card-reader slots in WoR-PE

enabled.description: Offer separate administrator rename/password setup after IoT first boot using fingerprint-pinned SSH; no offline FFU account modification.

username.description: Desired name for the existing built-in IoT administrator; service/system accounts are excluded.

password.description: New IoT password (12-127 UTF-16 characters), used only by the GUI post-boot SSH step. Prefer the masked GUI field; configuration files store plaintext and must not be committed.

host.description: Pi local IP address or hostname for manual post-boot connection. Required when automaticAddress is false; retained but unused while automatic addressing is enabled. Editing never resolves or connects.

automaticAddress.description: Resolve the default IoT hostname minwinpc after Connect (recommended). Defaults to true when no host is specified; an existing explicit host defaults to manual. Does not configure DHCP or assign a static address.

currentUsername.description: Required current IoT administrator login, prefilled with the Microsoft factory username when unset. Cannot be blank or disabled by turning off personalization; separate from the desired new administrator name.

currentPassword.description: Required current IoT login password, prefilled with the Microsoft factory password when unset. Empty passwords are unsupported by the password-based IoT SSH flow. Prefer the masked Advanced Options field; configuration files store plaintext and must remain private.

languageSetup.description: Apply the selected IoT UI language under DefaultAccount during post-boot SSH personalization, verifying that the language is installed and reporting restart requirements.

language.description: IoT language tag. Empty inherits the shared host-language detection or desktop locale preference; explicit selections are preserved. No language pack is downloaded.

setupAccount.description: Whether to setup a local administrator account during setup

password.description: Password for optional local account (omit or leave empty in committed configs)

localeSetup.description: Whether to configure Windows locale and regional settings (enabled by default)

locale.description: Windows locale code (e.g. en-US or en-GB); leave empty to use the host locale or en-US

confirmIotErase.description: Explicit erase consent for non-interactive IoT Core deployment only. Ignored for inspection-only dry runs. Requires an explicitly selected safe whole disk.

wipeIotDrive.description: Zero and read-back every addressable sector of the selected safe drive before applying the verified IoT FFU. Slow, destructive and opt-in; requires confirmIotWipe plus normal erase consent. Not a secure erase or hardware repair.

confirmIotWipe.description: Separate explicit confirmation for a requested full-drive IoT wipe. GUI users confirm Wipe and Flash; automation must deliberately opt in. Dry runs never wipe.

dryRun.description: Whether to run in dry-run mode without writing to storage

verifyTls.description: Whether to verify TLS certificates during downloads

checkForUpdates.description: Whether to report a newer published release before setup work starts. The check is read-only and never modifies this installation.

noUpdate.description: Legacy inverse of checkForUpdates; true disables the release check

logFile.description: Optional custom path for installer output. Omit to use a timestamped log under the download directory's logs/ folder, with last-run.log refreshed for support.

notifications.description: How the GUI announces the end of a flash. Only the completion sound is selectable; a failure always uses the platform's own error sound.

playSound.description: Whether to play a sound when the flash finishes

showNotification.description: Whether to post a desktop notification when the flash finishes (macOS Notification Center, or notify-send on Linux)

sounds.description: Completion sound per host platform. A name this host cannot play falls back to the platform default.

macos.description: Name of a sound in /System/Library/Sounds (e.g. Glass, Hero, Ping, Submarine)

linux.description: freedesktop sound-theme event name (e.g. complete, bell, message)

windows.description: Reserved: Windows is not a supported host, so no sound is played there

system.description: Advanced overrides for project runtime metadata. Defaults live in src/config/metadata.json and are loaded by src/lib/metadata.sh; ordinary configs should usually omit this block.

peInstallerUrl.description: Download URL for WoR-PE installer package

peInstallerSha256.description: SHA-256 digest for WoR-PE installer package

uefiVerPi3.description: Selected Pi 3 UEFI tag, used when uefiUseLatest is false and as the latest-lookup fallback; Pi 3 defaults to latest stable

uefiVerPi4.description: Selected Pi 4 UEFI tag, used when latest is disabled and as the latest-lookup fallback

uefiVerPi5.description: Selected Pi 5 UEFI tag, used when latest is disabled and as the latest-lookup fallback

driverVer.description: Selected Windows driver release tag, used when latest is disabled and as the latest-lookup fallback

armv80MaxBuild.description: Maximum Windows build supported on ARMv8.0 hardware

exampleBid.description: Example build ID shown in prompts

armv80SafeBid.description: Recommended safe build ID for ARMv8.0 hardware

repoSlug.description: GitHub repository owner/repo slug checked for newer releases
